item.title: “And what, monks, is non-restraint? Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a…
item.description:
“And what, monks, is non-restraint? Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms, praises them, and dwells with lust for them, then that monk, monks, should understand: ‘I have fallen away from wholesome states.’ The Tathāgata calls this ‘falling away.’ … There are sounds cognizable by the ear … odors … tastes … touches … There are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk delights in those phenomena, praises them, and dwells with lust for them, then that monk should understand: ‘I have fallen away from wholesome states.’ The Tathāgata calls this ‘falling away.’ Thus, monks, is non-restraint.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.98

item.title: “Migajāla, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable … enticing. If a monk does not delight in them, does not praise them,…
item.description:
“Migajāla, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable … enticing. If a monk does not delight in them, does not praise them, and dwells without lust for them — then delight ceases. Migajāla, I say that with the cessation of delight, suffering ceases. Sounds … Odors … Tastes … Touches … Migajāla, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind … If a monk does not delight in them, does not praise them, and dwells without lust for them — then delight ceases. Migajāla, I say that with the cessation of delight, suffering ceases.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.64

item.title: “One who indulges in sexual intercourse, Forgetting the teaching, Falls into wrong conduct — That life is not noble. One who formerly lived alone, Now…
item.description:
“One who indulges in sexual intercourse,
Forgetting the teaching,
Falls into wrong conduct —
That life is not noble.

One who formerly lived alone,
Now falls into sexual intercourse —
Like a swerving chariot,
He is called a worldling, a low person.

The good reputation he once had
He now loses.
Seeing this, one should train
To abandon sexual intercourse.

Overcome by thoughts,
He broods like a poor man —
Hearing others’ reproach,
He becomes dejected.

Then he makes weapons,
Attacked by others’ words —
He becomes greatly greedy,
Grasping at false speech.

Called wise, living alone,
If he falls into sexual intercourse,
He sorrows like a fool.

Seeing this danger,
The sage, steadfast before and after,
Lives solitary,
Not practicing sexual intercourse.

Train in seclusion —
This is the supreme noble practice.
Do not think yourself best,
Though you are close to Nibbāna.

The sage’s way is empty,
Not wishing for sensuality.
The one who has crossed the flood,
Envied and desired by people
Bound by sensual pleasures.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 4.7
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, form is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering. What is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it actually is with…
item.description:
“Monks, form is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering. What is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it actually is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Feeling … perception … formations … consciousness is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering. What is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it actually is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing thus, monks, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form … with feeling … with perception … with formations … with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. In liberation, knowledge arises: ‘Liberated.’ He knows: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’

Happy indeed are the arahants,
In them no craving is found,
Conceit has been cut off,
The net of delusion is torn apart.

They have attained the imperturbable,
Their minds are far from defilement,
They are not stained in the world —
The holy ones, free from defilements.

Fully understanding the five aggregates,
Practicing the seven good qualities,
Praised by true persons,
Disciples of the Buddha.

Possessing seven treasures,
Completed in the three trainings,
The great heroes wander forth,
Having abandoned all fear.

Endowed with ten powers,
The great elephant is concentrated,
They are supreme in the world,
Craving has been destroyed.

Achieved the knowledge of the adept,
This body is their last,
The end of the holy life,
Achieved independently.

Not shaken by perceptions,
Liberated from renewed existence,
Having reached the tamed state,
They are conquerors in the world.

Above, below, and across,
They have no delight,
They roar the lion’s roar —
The supreme Buddhas in the world!

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.76
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Householder, suppose a vulture, a kite, or a hawk seizes a piece of meat and flies up. Then other vultures, kites, or hawks chase after…
item.description:
“Householder, suppose a vulture, a kite, or a hawk seizes a piece of meat and flies up. Then other vultures, kites, or hawks chase after it, attacking and tearing at that piece of meat. What do you think, householder? If that vulture, kite, or hawk does not quickly let go of that piece of meat, would it thereby meet death or deadly suffering?” “Yes, venerable sir.” … “So too, householder, a noble disciple reflects: ‘The Blessed One has said that sensual pleasures are like a piece of meat — of much suffering, much despair, and the peril is even greater.’ Having seen this as it actually is with perfect wisdom, having abandoned the equanimity based on diversity … he cultivates such equanimity.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 54 – Potaliyasutta

item.title: Where the mind is restrained, There suffering ends. If the mind is fully restrained, One is fully freed from suffering. (The Blessed One): One should…
item.description:
Where the mind is restrained,
There suffering ends.
If the mind is fully restrained,
One is fully freed from suffering.

(The Blessed One):
One should not restrain the mind
Completely in every way.
Do not restrain the mind
When self-control is attained.
Where evil states arise,
There one should restrain the mind.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.24
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Furthermore, monks, one sees that woman’s corpse thrown in a charnel ground — with skeleton still connected, still having flesh and blood, held together by…
item.description:
“Furthermore, monks, one sees that woman’s corpse thrown in a charnel ground — with skeleton still connected, still having flesh and blood, held together by sinews … with skeleton still connected, without flesh but smeared with blood, held together by sinews … without flesh, without blood, held together by sinews … disconnected bones scattered here and there — here a hand bone, here a foot bone, here a shin bone, here a thigh bone, here a hip bone, here a back bone, here a skull. What do you think, monks? Has her former charm and beauty disappeared and peril become evident?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Thus, monks, is the peril in the case of forms.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 13 – Mahādukkhakkhandhasutta

item.title: Elder Māluṅkyaputta: One who lives heedlessly, Craving grows like a creeper. He drifts and wanders, Life after life, Like a monkey in the forest, Longing…
item.description:
Elder Māluṅkyaputta:

One who lives heedlessly,
Craving grows like a creeper.
He drifts and wanders,
Life after life,
Like a monkey in the forest,
Longing for fruit.

This wretched craving
Poisons the whole world.
When it conquers anyone,
Sorrow increases —
Like birana grass
Spreading and growing.

One who subdues craving,
Wretched, hard to conquer —
Sorrow falls from that person
Like a water drop from a lotus.

You have come here —
I teach this good thing.
Dig up the root of craving
Like seeking the sweet root
Of the usīra grass.
Do not let Māra, the flood,
Destroy you like a reed,
Again and again, forever.

Practice the Buddha’s instruction.
Do not let the moment pass.
If the moment passes, sorrow,
You will suffer in hell.

Heedlessness is dust,
Filthy dust born of heedlessness.
Heedful, with clear wisdom,
Pull out the dart from yourself.

From: Theragāthā 6.5
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Vaṅgīsa: Sensual desire burns me! My mind is on fire. Good indeed, Gotama — Out of compassion, speak The Dhamma that extinguishes the blaze.…
item.description:
Elder Vaṅgīsa:

Sensual desire burns me!
My mind is on fire.
Good indeed, Gotama —
Out of compassion, speak
The Dhamma that extinguishes the blaze.

It is because of distorted perception
That your mind is on fire.
Abandon the sign of the beautiful
That leads to sensual desire.

See formations as impermanent,
Suffering, not-self —
Extinguish great sensual desire —
Do not be burned again and again.
Develop the mind on foulness,
One-pointed, well-concentrated.
Practice mindfulness of the body,
Practice much disenchantment.

Practice the signless,
Destroy the underlying tendency to conceit.
By thoroughly penetrating conceit,
Your practice will be at peace.

From: Theragāthā 21.1
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Those who live in the world Without restraining sensual desires, Not abandoning passion, Enjoying sensual pleasures — They go to birth and aging, Again and…
item.description:
Those who live in the world
Without restraining sensual desires,
Not abandoning passion,
Enjoying sensual pleasures —
They go to birth and aging,
Again and again,
Bound by craving,
They go with the stream.
Therefore the wise,
Mindful in the world,
Do not enjoy sensual pleasures,
Do not do evil deeds.
Even if they suffer,
Abandoning sensual pleasures,
They are called those
Who go against the stream.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.5
